title: Mukesh Kumar Dubey v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Prashant Kumar, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner may clear clause 4.1 dues, connection thereafter as per law
headnote: Writ seeking a new electricity connection at premises said to carry outstanding dues disposed of. The petitioner may clear the outstanding amount under clause 4.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Electricity Department may then provide the connection in accordance with law.
facts: Mukesh Kumar Dubey approached the Allahabad High Court for a direction that the respondents release a new electricity connection at House No. 416, Kaparphorawa, Varanasi. The Electricity Department resisted the prayer on the ground that electricity dues were outstanding against the premises. Its counsel told the Court that, until those dues were deposited, Clause 4.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 stood in the way of a new connection, and that payment would remove the difficulty.

holding_units.topic: new connection where premises dues are outstanding
holding_units.holding: A writ for a new connection at premises carrying outstanding electricity dues need not be kept pending. The petitioner is at liberty to clear the outstanding amount as per clause 4.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Electricity Department may thereafter provide the connection on the premises in accordance with law.
holding_units.flag: Cited as clause 4.1, without naming the fourth proviso.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench disposed of the writ for an immediate new connection by leaving the petitioner to clear outstanding dues on the premises under clause 4.1, after which the Electricity Department may provide the connection in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Quantum of the outstanding dues and whether they were payable by the petitioner
not_decided.note: The Court did not quantify the dues or adjudicate liability. Clearance, and any connection thereafter, was left to be worked out in accordance with law.
